blocks.heading: Compare the Practical Paths
blocks.sourceSectionTitle: First, which result do you have?

rows: Compartment (failed one or two subjects)
On a CBSE circular of 30 May 2024, quoted by the Delhi High Court on 9 July 2025, a student placed in compartment can apply for the supplementary exam in one subject.
Apply for the supplementary exam through your school. CBSE held the 2026 Class 12 supplementary exam on 15 July, as reported, and dates change each year.
Essential repeat (failed three or more main subjects)
In the Delhi High Court case, a student who failed three of five main theory subjects was placed in Essential Repeat and could not take the supplementary exam.
Repeat the year in your school, appear as a private candidate where the board allows it, or move to NIOS.
Passed theory but failed practical or internal marks
The court read CBSE bye-law 40.1 to mean 33 percent in theory and 33 percent in practical or internal assessment are needed separately. A good internal grade alone does not give a pass certificate.
Ask your school exactly which component you failed, and ask whether the supplementary exam covers it.
State board result (PUC, Intermediate, Plus Two, HSC)
State boards run their own supplementary exams. The name, dates and number of subjects differ, so the CBSE rules above do not carry over.
Read your own board's circular. Tamil Nadu officials, for example, said in 2023 that tens of thousands of failed students did not apply for the supplementary test.
Who can join

Secondary needs Class VIII passed and proof of age 14. Senior secondary does not allow direct admission, and you must have passed Secondary from a recognised board and be at least 15 on 31 July of the admission year.
Credit for what you passed

Learners from other boards can transfer up to two subjects passed in the last five years, if those subjects are in the NIOS scheme. Transfer of credit must be requested at admission, with the original marksheet.
Pass rule
A pass needs at least five subjects, including one or at most two languages, with at least 33 percent in the external exam and 33 percent in aggregate.
Exam timing
On-demand exams are held monthly at regional centres after the first public exam. You choose the date and subject, and you only sit the subjects still to clear.
Cost anchor
The NIOS FAQ lists Rs 250 per theory subject and Rs 100 per practical for an on-demand exam. Fees change, so check the current table before you pay.
Recognition

NIOS says its certificates have the same recognition as other boards, and the Association of Indian Universities has granted equivalence for higher studies. Part admission gives only a marksheet, not a certificate.

blocks.heading: ITI Through Your Class 10 Certificate
blocks.sourceSectionTitle: Diploma and ITI through your Class 10 certificate

rows: Engineering diploma (polytechnic)
In the Nagaland directorate's rules, Class 10 with Maths and Science passed. Rules differ by state, and admission is by merit.
Three-year course. Diploma holders may enter the second year of engineering through lateral entry, which Nagaland caps at 10 percent of intake over the approved seats.
ITI trade (CTS)
Most trades ask for Class 10, Dress Making for Class 8, with a minimum age of 14 and no upper limit, on the DGT page for NSTI Indore.
Most trades run one year, and Electronics Mechanic runs two. NCVT awards the National Trade Certificate after the exam, with 80 percent attendance.
ITI then diploma then degree
A 2023 Tamil Nadu report said ITI completers can enter a second-year diploma directly, and diploma holders can join second-year engineering degrees.
A ladder that starts from Class 10, if your state and seats allow it. Check each step's rule before you plan.
Fashion, interior and other diplomas
The Nagaland rules name fashion and interior and architecture assistantship diplomas for Class 10 pass students, with Maths and Science for some.
Skill-based work in design and construction. Check recognition and placement before you pay.
Government jobs
A written-exam rank high enough to be called for the next round.
A later stage such as a skill test, interview or document check, then a posting you may not choose.
ITI to diploma to degree ladder
A good ITI result and a seat under the state's limited lateral-entry quota.
Engineering-level maths and coursework in the second year, which catches students who skipped the basics.
Software and design without a degree
Getting your first paid project or job from a stranger.
Moving from small gigs to steady, better-paid work, which depends on repeat clients and a visible track record.
